summary: ACCEPT. The three owed guards on #831 and #832, and all three are genuine ONE-VARIABLE CONTROLLED PAIRS - each mutant turns the test red, each passes unmutated, verified by execution. G1: reverting the latch to file-existence gives 1 failed, and it fails for the RIGHT reason - under the mutant the canonical report stays partial, the notified marker is absent, and curl is invoked with an EMPTY verdict line, which is the described harm rather than an incidental break. G2: inverting the gate from fail-open to fail-closed gives 1 failed on the resubmit count, with the captured log showing [OMS-CANCEL-UNCONFIRMED] reads_failed=1 dead_target_bound=1 - the FRTT unowned-working-order shape returning while wearing the opposite label. G3: deleting the abandon call gives 1 failed on 'submitted' == 'cancelled', the stuck intent that occupies the #644 composition cap. ⭐ G2's call trace is confirmed BY CAUSATION, not by grep: the test calls _verify_cancel_landed directly, _record_cancel_verify_reports appears nowhere in it, and the mutant I applied lives ONLY inside _verify_cancel_landed yet turned the test red - so the wrong-function-under-test defect that created this guard is genuinely fixed. G3's ordering is right: the terminal event is seeded and committed BEFORE the single drift pass, and zero broker submissions ever occur, so it bounds on the FIRST pass rather than passing on an unbounded one. G1 genuinely EXECUTES the wrapper via subprocess rather than grepping its source, the seeded report is truly partial (non-empty but lacking the VERDICT line, so it exercises the grep half of report_complete), and the date is pinned via MAI_TAI_EOD_TEST_DAY rather than the wall clock so there is no time bomb. ⭐ All three names describe what they actually assert - and the renamed G2 test DROPPED the old 'without inventing evidence' claim it no longer tests, which is the honest move and the opposite of the defect it fixes. Scope clean: two test files, no production change, extract verified byte-identical to the HEAD blobs after restore. NON-BLOCKING follow-up: a coverage regression rides along, because the replaced test was the ONLY one in the repo referencing _record_cancel_verify_reports - deleting its 'if order is None: return' guard now survives the entire suite at 2697 passed. It survives even the new G2 test because the caller wraps the call in except Exception, so the AttributeError is swallowed into [OMS-CANCEL-RESUBMIT-RAISED] and the cancel-count assertion still passes. Latent, not live - HEAD's guard is present and correct - but if it were removed, verifier resubmit replies would silently stop feeding the durable dead-target budget while the log said only 'resubmit raised'. Two-line fix: assert that _record_cancel_verify_reports with a missing target_order_id writes no BrokerOrderEvent. COSMETIC: the G3 test seeds symbol=BOUNDED but inherits client_order_id=LASE-target-1, so the log reads symbol=BOUNDED target_client_order_id=LASE-target-1.
